title: Blue Gates and Fortified Churches: A Slow Week Through Saxon Transylvania
subRegion: Târnava Mare & the Hârtibaciu Plateau, Saxon Transylvania (Siebenbürgen)

bestPeriod.window: the second half of May into June (hay meadows in flower), and late September
bestPeriod.avoid: November-March (village guesthouses close, unpaved commune roads turn to mud) and the first week of August

hook: Seven days, four beds, and a lot of standing still. This is the Târnava Mare plateau: villages laid out by German settlers in the 12th century, each with one long street, one fortified church and a hill of hay meadow behind it. You will wait for a woman with a key, eat at a shared table with whoever else is staying, and be overtaken by a horse cart. If you need three sights a day, this is the wrong week. If you want to hear cowbells at dusk, it is exactly right.

snapshot.Best period: Second half of May-June; late September
snapshot.Start / End: Sighișoara → Sibiu (one-way, ~120 km total driving across the week)
snapshot.Getting there: Fly to Sibiu (SBZ) or Târgu Mureș (TGM); Cluj (CLJ) is the bigger hub, 2h30 by car. Rail: Bucharest-Sighișoara ~5h on the CFR IR line, Brașov-Sighișoara ~2h30. Hire the car in Sibiu and drop it there on Day 7.

itinerary.title: Into the Citadel
itinerary.morning: Arrive and park below the walls, the citadel is pedestrian-priority and the lanes are cobbled. Settle in, then walk up through the Tailors' Tower into **Piața Cetății**.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Clock Tower** (Turnul cu Ceas), the 1648 figure mechanism, the guild museum inside and the gallery at the top over the tiled roofs. Then the **Scholars' Stairs** (Scara Școlarilor), 175 covered wooden steps of 1642, up to the Church on the Hill and the German cemetery behind it.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **La Fabrica de Bere** below the citadel. Walk back up in the dark; the lanes are lit and empty by 21:00.

itinerary.title: Saschiz, Criț and the Blue Pattern
itinerary.morning: East on the DN13 to **Saschiz**, the 1493 fortified church with its clock tower modelled on Sighișoara's, and the ruined **Peasant Citadel** on the hill above, a 25-minute climb through orchard.
itinerary.afternoon: Buy cobalt-blue slipware at the **Saschiz ceramics** workshop at village prices, then 12 km south to **Criț** (Deutsch-Kreuz), a hall church inside a ring wall, ringed by some of the most botanically rich hay meadows in Europe.
itinerary.evening: Back to Sighișoara for a slow supper, and pack.

itinerary.title: The Road to Viscri
itinerary.morning: Drive south-east via Bunești and turn onto the commune road to **Viscri**. The last 6 km were long notorious for gravel and have been substantially upgraded, but check conditions after rain.
itinerary.afternoon: The **fortified church**, UNESCO-listed, Romanesque core of about 1100, a defensive ring with a bacon tower where families still hung their smoked pork. Climb the tower. Then walk the street, gate by cobalt gate, to **Gheorghe Mihai's forge**.
itinerary.evening: Shared-table dinner at your **Mihai Eminescu Trust** house: soup, a stew, home-made *pălincă*, everyone at one table. Lights out early; there is no light pollution here at all.

itinerary.title: Viscri Standing Still
itinerary.morning: Buy felt slippers at the church gate where the cooperative sells them, then take a **horse cart** out to the hill pastures above the village, the standard village outing, about 90 minutes, arranged through your host.
itinerary.afternoon: The village museum room, the buffalo herd coming home to the well, an hour on a bench. This day is deliberately empty.
itinerary.evening: Second shared dinner. Ask your host about the 1990 emigration, almost the entire Saxon population of these villages left for Germany within two years, and every family here has that story.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km on foot or by cart

itinerary.title: Biertan, Copșa Mare and Richiș
itinerary.morning: West to **Biertan**, the grandest of the fortified churches, UNESCO, three defensive rings, the covered stair up from the square, and the **sacristy door with its 19-bolt lock**, worked by a single key and shown at the 1900 Paris exposition. The *matrimonial prison* tower, where couples seeking divorce were locked in together with one bed, one plate and one spoon, is genuine.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the ridge to **Copșa Mare**, a near-abandoned village with an oversized Gothic church, then 4 km on to **Richiș** and its unexpectedly refined church interior with carved capitals.
itinerary.evening: **Casa Vale ke Vino** in Richiș, dinner at the long table with the house's own and regional wines.

itinerary.title: Mălâncrav and the Apple Orchards
itinerary.morning: North to **Mălâncrav**, which held the largest surviving Saxon community in the region. The church has the best-preserved medieval wall paintings in Transylvania, 14th-century, in the chancel; the key is held in the village.
itinerary.afternoon: **Apafi Manor**, the Mihai Eminescu Trust's restored 17th-century manor house, and the traditional orchards below it, whose apples become the juice sold across the region. Then back to Richiș the slow way.
itinerary.evening: Last village dinner. Settle up in cash, several of these houses still prefer it.

itinerary.title: Down to Sibiu
itinerary.morning: Drive to **Sibiu** via Mediaș. Park outside the old town and walk into **Piața Mare**, the Brukenthal Palace, the Council Tower (Turnul Sfatului) and the eyelid dormer windows that watch you from every roof.
itinerary.afternoon: **Piața Mică** and the **Bridge of Lies**, the Lutheran cathedral, then either the Brukenthal Museum's old masters or the open-air **ASTRA Museum**, which needs two hours.
itinerary.evening: Dinner on Piața Mică, drop the car, fly out of Sibiu or take the morning train.

accommodationStrategy.name: Mihai Eminescu Trust guesthouse
accommodationStrategy.description: restored with lime plaster, local oak and tiled stoves rather than converted into hotels, with the income going back into the village. Half board at a shared table, 200 m from the fortified church.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6-10 weeks ahead through the Trust's own booking channel, longer for May and September weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Casa Vale ke Vino
accommodationStrategy.description: a restored Saxon house with a working cellar, a real list of Transylvanian producers and a host who cooks, and Biertan, Copșa Mare and Mălâncrav are all inside 20 km.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4-8 weeks ahead direct; confirm dinner when you reserve, since it is cooked to numbers.

accommodationStrategy.name: A citadel guesthouse in Sighișoara
accommodationStrategy.description: sleeping inside the walls gives you the citadel at 07:00 and 22:00, before and after the Brașov coaches. Ask about parking below the Tailors' Tower.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4-6 weeks ahead; avoid the last weekend of July, when the Medieval Festival fills every bed in town.

logistics.connectivity: good, 4G reaches most villages; Viscri's thick-walled houses block it indoors.
logistics.emergency: 112. Nearest hospitals Sighișoara and Sibiu; carry a basic kit.
logistics.weather: continental plateau at 400-600 m. Thunderstorms build fast on May and June afternoons and turn commune roads greasy within twenty minutes. Mornings are cold into early June.
logistics.bookingWindows: guesthouses 4-10 weeks; church keys need no booking but do need someone to be home, call ahead through your host for Mălâncrav and Copșa Mare, which are not permanently staffed.
logistics.money: Romanian leu, roughly **€1 ≈ 4.95-5.05 RON**. Cards work in Sighișoara and Sibiu; in the villages, in the craft cooperatives and for church keys, cash only. Draw €150, €200 in RON before leaving Sighișoara. Church-key custodians expect 10-20 RON (€2, €4) per person, which is not a tip but the maintenance fund.
logistics.transportRules: you need a car; rural bus links between these villages are effectively non-existent. Romania requires a **rovinietă** road vignette for national roads, hire cars normally include it, but confirm at pickup. Drink-driving limit is zero. Watch for horse carts without reflectors after dusk and for shepherd dogs on the meadow tracks.
logistics.permits: the fortified churches are working Lutheran parish property, not state museums; opening is at the custodian's discretion. Dress modestly, do not fly a drone over the church rings, and ask before photographing people at work.

proTips: Ask your Viscri host to arrange the **horse cart** the evening before, not on the morning. The carts double as working transport and are committed early.
In Sighișoara, walk the citadel between **07:30 and 09:00**. The coach groups from Brașov arrive around 10:30 and leave by 16:00; the town is entirely yours on either side of that.
Say the words: *"Cheia, vă rog"*, "the key, please." At Copșa Mare, Mălâncrav, Criț and Richiș the church is locked and a neighbour has the key. A house number is usually posted on the gate.

Book **half board** everywhere you can. Village restaurants barely exist here, the guesthouse dinner is better than anything you would drive to, and the shared table is the actual social content of the week.
Buy the **Saschiz ceramics in Saschiz** and the **felt slippers in Viscri**, not in Sibiu's Piața Mică, where the same objects carry a 60-100% markup.
Drive nothing after dark on the commune roads. Unlit carts, loose cattle and unmarked culverts make the 20 km from Biertan to Richiș a different road at 22:00 than at 18:00.
With one spare hour in Sibiu, walk the **Pasajul Scărilor** down from the upper town instead of entering a museum, free, and the city's best-preserved medieval fabric.

raw.Village squares and centres by name: **Piața Cetății** in Sighișoara, the small trapezoid inside the citadel where the Clock Tower, Casa Vlad Dracul and the Scholars' Stairs all meet. **Viscri's** single unpaved street, widening around the fortified church and the well, with the famous **blue gates**, the cobalt-painted double doors that the village agreed to keep. **Biertan's** village square below its three-ringed church hill. **Saschiz's** roadside centre on the DN13 under the Peasant Citadel. **Richiș's** wide green street. **Sibiu's** three-square spine: **Piața Mare**, **Piața Mică** and the **Bridge of Lies** (Podul Minciunilor, 1859, the first cast-iron bridge in Romania) between them.
raw.Market days and artisan specialities: **Sighișoara's** daily covered market off Str. Târnavei is at its fullest on Friday and Saturday mornings; the regional livestock and goods fairs at **Agnita** and **Rupea** run to a monthly or weekly commune calendar rather than a tourist one. Craft is the real reason to be here: **Viscri's felt-slipper cooperative**, where roughly thirty village women knit and felt wool slippers sold from the church gate and by the Mihai Eminescu Trust; **Saschiz's cobalt-blue ceramics**, the revived Saschiz pattern of blue-on-white slipware fired in the village; and **blacksmith Gheorghe Mihai** in Viscri, whose forge at the top of the street makes hinges, hooks, gate ironwork and the horseshoe nails everything else runs on. Buy at the source, the margin goes into the village.
raw.Boutique and characterful stays: the **Mihai Eminescu Trust houses in Viscri**, restored Saxon farmhouses (No. 32, No. 63 and others) let with lime-plastered walls, tiled stoves, no televisions and breakfast from village eggs. **Casa Vale ke Vino** in Richiș, a wine-focused guesthouse in a restored Saxon house with a cellar and a long table. **Casa Bunicii** for a traditional Transylvanian dinner and rooms in the Sighișoara/Saschiz area. **La Fabrica de Bere** in Sighișoara, the old brewery building below the citadel, for a proper sit-down meal.
raw.Deliberate slow-travel pacing (max one r: four bases, three relocations, none longer than 55 km. **Sighișoara nights 1-2 → Viscri nights 3-4 → Richiș nights 5-6 → Sibiu night 7.** Legs are Sighișoara-Viscri 42 km (~1h), Viscri-Richiș 48 km (~1h15 including the Biertan detour), Richiș-Sibiu 55 km (~1h10). Everything else is on foot, and the local speed limit is set by horse carts, not by the DN14. The evening custom in these guesthouses is a **shared table**, one dinner, one sitting, served at a fixed hour to everyone staying. Say yes. It is the best food of the week and the only way you meet anyone.
